hunks.baseline: I won’t say the fight with Ma Sanbao was fiercer and more difficult than any I’d ever fought.
hunks.sol: I won’t say the fight with Ma Sanbao was fiercer or harder than any I’d ever fought.

hunks.baseline: There had been plenty of stronger opponents in the hellish battlefields I’d fought my way through. Even now, I could name several who’d been far worse than him.
hunks.sol: I’d faced plenty of worse opponents in the hellish battles I’d fought my way through. I could name several right now.

hunks.baseline: The System was practically sealed, and my body—wrecked by the aftereffects of One Annihilation—wouldn’t move the way I wanted it to.
hunks.sol: The System was practically sealed, and my body, wrecked by the aftereffects of One Annihilation, wouldn’t move the way I wanted it to.

hunks.baseline: And yet, at this very moment, I was the one standing on two feet.
hunks.sol: Even so, I was the one still standing.

hunks.baseline: In this merciless world ruled by the law of the jungle, Ma Sanbao had made a mistake. A small one, but a fatal one.
hunks.sol: In this merciless world ruled by the law of the jungle, Ma Sanbao had made a small but fatal mistake.

hunks.baseline: I whispered as I looked into Ma Sanbao’s hollow eyes. Then I drove the short spear through his throat even deeper.
hunks.sol: I looked into Ma Sanbao’s empty eyes as I whispered, then drove the short spear deeper through his throat.

hunks.baseline: *Squish. Crack.*
hunks.sol: *Crunch. Crack.*

hunks.baseline: Only after the spear had severed his carotid artery and slid along his collarbone to somewhere near his heart did I let go. At last free of my grip, Ma Sanbao’s body slowly tilted over.
hunks.sol: I didn’t let go until the spear had severed his carotid artery and followed his collarbone down toward his heart. Freed from my grip at last, Ma Sanbao’s body slowly toppled.

hunks.baseline: Along with the spear buried deep in him like a tree root.
hunks.sol: The spear remained buried deep inside him like a tree root.

hunks.baseline: There was no System message saying I’d defeated an enemy. No clear, familiar chime, either.
hunks.sol: There was no System message telling me I’d defeated an enemy. No clear, familiar chime.

hunks.baseline: I stared at the corpse lying motionless in a pool of blood, panting, then let out a shout charged with internal energy.
hunks.sol: Panting, I stared at the corpse lying motionless in a pool of blood, then let out a shout charged with internal energy.

hunks.baseline: Before anyone could even grasp what that shout meant, I charged back into the battlefield, where swords and spears clashed.
hunks.sol: Before anyone could grasp what that meant, I plunged back into the battlefield, where swords and spears were flying.

hunks.baseline: *Whoosh! Thud!*
hunks.sol: *Whoosh! Crunch!*

hunks.baseline: Short, simple movements. Only the bare minimum of internal energy.
hunks.sol: Short, simple movements. The bare minimum of internal energy.

hunks.baseline: The face of a man muttering those eight words like a mantra—“Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in reverence”—caved in.
hunks.sol: I crushed the face of a man muttering those eight words like a mantra—“Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in reverence.” I was sick of hearing them.

hunks.baseline: I jerked my head aside, avoiding the blades that flew in from both sides of the collapsing corpse, its features mangled beyond recognition.
hunks.sol: As his body crumpled, its features mangled beyond recognition, blades flew at me from either side. I jerked my head out of their path.

hunks.baseline: The two blades that had missed me by a hand’s breadth struck each other. Ignoring the vibrations reaching my ears, I thrust out my hand, its grip torn to ribbons.
hunks.sol: The two blades missed me by a hand’s breadth and struck each other. Ignoring the vibration ringing in my ears, I thrust out my torn hand.

hunks.baseline: Compressed air, heated until it glowed, burst outward.
hunks.sol: Hot, compressed air burst outward.

hunks.baseline: The Flame Divine Palm I unleashed held only three-tenths of my internal energy. Even so, the force and heat packed into that palm strike were enough to kill all but the most exceptional Peak masters on the spot.
hunks.sol: I’d put only three-tenths of my internal energy into the Flame Divine Palm. Even so, the force and heat of that strike were enough to kill most Peak masters on the spot.

hunks.baseline: “Gah—!”
hunks.sol: “Gah…!”

hunks.baseline: The man’s body flew backward, spraying dark red blood.
hunks.sol: The man flew backward, spraying dark red blood.

hunks.baseline: But whether that nameless enemy lived or died was no longer my concern. What he’d left behind was another matter.
hunks.sol: Whether that nameless enemy lived or died was no longer my concern. What he’d left behind was another matter.

hunks.baseline: The sword had already slipped from its owner’s grasp. I caught the hilt smoothly and swung it in one motion.
hunks.sol: His sword had already slipped from his hand. I caught the hilt and swung it in one smooth motion.

hunks.baseline: Space split open. Flames coiled around the blade, scorching the air, flesh, and bone.
hunks.sol: Space split open. Flames wrapped around the blade, heating the air and burning flesh and bone.

hunks.baseline: Simple, but fast. And so powerful it couldn’t be stopped.
hunks.sol: Simple and swift. Too powerful to stop.

hunks.baseline: At the end of it were the enemies’ blood and screams.
hunks.sol: And at the end of it came my enemies’ blood and screams.

hunks.baseline: I pushed forward, drenched in blood spraying like a fountain. I dodged the countless blades crashing in from every direction, knocked them aside, then sent them flying right back where they came from.
hunks.sol: I pushed forward, drenched in blood spraying like a fountain. I dodged the countless blades coming at me from every direction, knocked them aside, then sent the attacks right back.

hunks.baseline: When the sword broke, I used a spear. When the spear snapped, I used an ax or a dagger.
hunks.sol: When the sword broke, I used a spear. When the spear snapped, an ax or a dagger.

hunks.baseline: If I had nothing else, I used arms and legs harder than steel.
hunks.sol: And if I had none of those, I used arms and legs harder than steel.

hunks.baseline: *Grit!*
hunks.sol: *Crunch!*

hunks.baseline: There was no need to reach for some grand concept like all streams returning to the sea.
hunks.sol: There was no need to invoke some grand concept like all streams returning to the sea.

hunks.baseline: To me, martial arts were a chain of points and lines.
hunks.sol: To me, martial arts were connections between countless points and lines.

hunks.baseline: If your life was on the line, you used every means at your disposal.
hunks.sol: When your life was on the line, you couldn’t afford to rule out any means.

hunks.baseline: If it could kill the enemy as quickly and reliably as possible, the shape of the weapon didn’t matter.
hunks.sol: If a weapon could kill an enemy as quickly and surely as possible, its shape didn’t matter.

hunks.baseline: The enemies kept pouring in, their lips endlessly murmuring those mantra-like words, no matter how many I killed. But I could see the emotion rising in their eyes.
hunks.sol: The enemies kept blocking my way, no matter how many I killed. Their lips never stopped murmuring those mantra-like words, but I could see the emotion in their eyes.

hunks.baseline: I struggled to suppress my ragged breathing. Every muscle in my body throbbed as if I’d been electrocuted, and the hand that had gripped Ma Sanbao’s sword could barely feel pain anymore.
hunks.sol: I fought to keep my ragged breathing quiet. Every muscle in my body throbbed as if I’d been electrocuted, and the hand that had grabbed Ma Sanbao’s sword could barely feel pain anymore.

hunks.baseline: After pulling something that crazy, I was probably in terrible shape.
hunks.sol: After pulling something that crazy, it was probably a terrible sight.

hunks.baseline: Wolves hunted in packs, but no matter how hungry they were, they couldn’t bare their teeth at a lion that roared and charged at them.
hunks.sol: Wolves hunted in packs, but no matter how hungry they were, they couldn’t bare their teeth at a lion that roared and charged them.

hunks.baseline: They only tried to sink their teeth into a lion’s nape when it started backing away.
hunks.sol: They only tried to sink their teeth into its neck when it backed away.

hunks.baseline: My heavy footstep sent the blood pooled around my ankles rippling.
hunks.sol: My heavy step sent the blood pooled around my ankles rippling.

hunks.baseline: Like the blood still seeping from the countless wounds carved into my body, the blood reflecting the night sky was dark red.
hunks.sol: Like the blood seeping from the wounds all over my body, the blood beneath the night sky was dark red.

hunks.baseline: Suddenly, I felt exhausted to my very bones.
hunks.sol: A wave of exhaustion hit me.

hunks.baseline: I’d killed well over a hundred of them, by my rough count, and still the enemies filled my field of vision.
hunks.sol: I’d killed over a hundred of them by my rough count, yet enemies still filled my view.

hunks.baseline: The Great Nation’s—no, Dark Heaven’s—elite troops. Every one of them was at least Supreme First Rate, some nearing the peak of Peak.
hunks.sol: The Great Nation’s—no, Dark Heaven’s—elite. They ranged from Supreme First Rate to the upper reaches of Peak. Each one was skilled, and each worshiped the Lord of Heaven like a fanatic.

hunks.baseline: I had to defeat them all, every last fanatic who worshiped the Lord of Heaven, before I could reach Jeok Cheongang, who was still fighting a thunderous battle that seemed like it would never end.
hunks.sol: I had to get through them all to reach Jeok Cheongang. His earth-shaking battle was still going on, and it felt as though it might never end.

hunks.baseline: Even as we gained the upper hand without the Emperor’s help, why did one corner of my heart keep trembling with unease?
hunks.sol: We were gaining the upper hand without the Emperor’s help, so why did unease still gnaw at me?

hunks.baseline: Why did that storm-clouded night sky feel so ominous?
hunks.sol: Why did that cloud-choked night sky look so ominous?

hunks.baseline: No. I did know.
hunks.sol: No. I knew.

hunks.baseline: *This isn’t over.*
hunks.sol: *This isn’t all of it.*

hunks.baseline: No matter how I looked, I couldn’t see them. The assassins who should have been protecting the Emperor. The twin Supreme Peak masters who’d served as the gatekeepers of Qianqing Palace.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t see them anywhere, no matter how I looked: the assassins who were supposed to protect the Emperor, or the twin Supreme Peak masters who had guarded Qianqing Palace.

hunks.baseline: Even the Embroidered Uniform Guards in this great banquet hall numbered only half as many as I knew to be here.
hunks.sol: Even the number of Embroidered Uniform Guards in the Grand Banquet Hall was only half what I knew it should be.

hunks.baseline: *And it’s the same for Cang Gong.*
hunks.sol: *And the same goes for Cang Gong.*

hunks.baseline: The two men had crossed a point of no return, yet neither had revealed all their forces. No doubt they were holding back their cards, waiting for the other to make the first move.
hunks.sol: The two men had crossed a point of no return, yet neither had revealed all his forces. They had to be concealing their moves, waiting for the other to show his hand first.

hunks.baseline: Even if the entire imperial capital had split in two by now, locked in a bloody battle, I wouldn’t have been surprised.
hunks.sol: I wouldn’t have been surprised if the entire Imperial Capital had split in two by now and was fighting a bloody battle.

hunks.baseline: This was a shitty situation.
hunks.sol: What a shitty mess.

hunks.baseline: But even so, I had to fight.
hunks.sol: Even so, I had to fight.

hunks.baseline: I had to survive the Dark Heaven dogs charging at me beneath a rain of arrows—and the Emperor and So Gyo, whose allegiance I couldn’t even guess.
hunks.sol: The Dark Heaven dogs charging beneath that rain of arrows weren’t the only ones I had to survive. There were also the Emperor and So Gyo, and I didn’t even know whether they were enemies or allies.

hunks.baseline: I turned my head and looked at the raised platform in the distance.
hunks.sol: I turned toward the high platform in the distance.

hunks.baseline: Baek Yeon and So Gyo.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The Emperor was watching the battlefield with those two Supreme Peak masters at his sides, each powerful enough to turn the tide of the battle in an instant.
hunks.sol: Baek Yeon and So Gyo stood on either side of the Emperor. With those two Supreme Peak masters, either of whom could turn the battle around in an instant, he watched the fighting.

hunks.baseline: I also saw Aehyang, surrounded by a handful of palace attendants, and the young king, kneeling for some reason.
hunks.sol: I could also see Aehyang surrounded by a handful of palace attendants, and the young king kneeling for some reason.

hunks.baseline: For just a moment, my attention was drawn to them. Then the countless whistles that had crossed the sky belatedly reached my ears.
hunks.sol: My gaze lingered on them for a moment. Only then did the countless whistles crossing the sky reach my ears.

hunks.baseline: A thick darkness spread over my head.
hunks.sol: A deep shadow fell over my head.

hunks.baseline: Hundreds of arrowheads flashed as they fell, all aimed at me alone. At the same moment, a red alarm bell rang violently inside my head.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of arrowheads flashed, all fired at me alone, and an alarm rang furiously inside my head.

hunks.baseline: I knew before I even moved.
hunks.sol: I knew before I moved.

hunks.baseline: Dodging all those arrows was next to impossible.
hunks.sol: Dodging them all would be next to impossible.

hunks.baseline: I was already exhausted. My body and senses had grown sluggish, and I was stranded in far too open a space to avoid every arrow shot by First Rate masters using their internal energy.
hunks.sol: I was exhausted. My body and senses had grown sluggish, and I stood isolated in an open space with nowhere to evade the countless arrows fired by First Rate masters using internal energy.

hunks.baseline: *I have to use as little strength as possible and avoid a fatal injury.*
hunks.sol: *Use as little strength as I can. Avoid anything fatal.*

hunks.baseline: I clenched my teeth, pulling an abandoned spear from the ground as I raised my remaining hand toward the sky.
hunks.sol: I gritted my teeth and pulled an abandoned spear from the ground. With my other hand, I reached toward the sky.

hunks.baseline: The air surrounding me trembled.
hunks.sol: The air around me trembled.

hunks.baseline: I’d avoided using my Middle Dantian except in the most dangerous situations, even during battle, to conserve my stamina. But now wasn’t the time to be picky about what was bitter and what was sweet.
hunks.sol: I’d avoided using my Middle Dantian during the fight unless the danger was extreme, conserving my stamina. Now wasn’t the time to care whether the medicine tasted bitter.

hunks.baseline: Even if it was bitter, I had to swallow it.
hunks.sol: Bitter or not, I had to swallow it.

hunks.baseline: I had to bear it myself.
hunks.sol: Bear the cost myself.

hunks.baseline: There was no way in hell I was going to fall here, of all places.
hunks.sol: I had no intention of falling here.

hunks.baseline: Just as I clenched my fist, ready to meet the arrows hurtling toward me with a ferocious whistle that seemed to tear through my ears—
hunks.sol: I was about to close my raised hand into a fist against the arrows screaming toward me when—

hunks.baseline: “Shield formation! Defend!”
hunks.sol: “Turtle Shell! Defend!”

hunks.baseline: At a familiar shout from somewhere, a group rushed in at lightning speed and surrounded me.
hunks.sol: At a shout from someone whose voice sounded familiar, a group swept in with blinding speed and surrounded me.

hunks.baseline: They held up massive shields.
hunks.sol: Massive shields led the way.

hunks.baseline: Sparks lit up the darkness. Countless broken and splintered arrow fragments scattered in every direction. A second rain of arrows came moments later, and dozens of crescent-bladed polearms flashed toward them.
hunks.sol: Sparks lit up the darkness. Broken arrow fragments scattered in every direction. Moments later, a second rain of arrows came, and dozens of crescent-bladed polearms flashed toward it.

hunks.baseline: Blade Force spread across the sky in brilliant half-moons.
hunks.sol: Blade Force swept across the sky in brilliant half-moons.

hunks.baseline: The powerful energy formed a kind of barrier, slicing apart every arrow that flew toward them. The scattered fragments couldn’t pierce the gaps in their golden armor.
hunks.sol: That powerful energy formed a barrier, cutting apart every incoming arrow. The fragments couldn’t find a way through the gaps in their golden armor.

hunks.baseline: Countless fragments lost their momentum and fell.
hunks.sol: Countless fragments fell, their force spent.

hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, answered without a hint of emotion.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, answered evenly.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t do it very often.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t say it very often.”

hunks.baseline: “I figured as much. I wasn’t expecting it in the first place.”
hunks.sol: “I thought not. I wasn’t expecting it.”

hunks.baseline: “When I owe someone a debt, I say thank you. Like now.”
hunks.sol: “When I owe someone, I thank them. Like now.”

hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun struck his golden armor with a military salute, then continued.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun struck his golden armor in a military salute. When he spoke again, his tone had changed.

hunks.baseline: His tone was different now. Respectful.

hunks.sol: “…Huh.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m sure you have plenty to ask me, and plenty you want to say. But I’d like you to save it until after this is over.”
hunks.sol: “I’m sure you have plenty to ask and plenty to say. But I’d like you to leave it until this is over.”

hunks.baseline: If he came out with something like that before I could even open my mouth, there was nothing left to say.
hunks.sol: What was I supposed to say when he got that out before I’d even opened my mouth?

hunks.baseline: I clicked my tongue quietly and looked toward the enemies pressing in from all sides.
hunks.sol: I clicked my tongue and watched the enemies pressing in from all sides.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, let me ask you one thing.”
hunks.sol: “Hey. One question.”

hunks.baseline: “At least His Majesty is. We are on your side.”
hunks.sol: “At least His Majesty is. We’re on your side.”

hunks.baseline: I immediately understood why he’d gone out of his way to add that qualifier.
hunks.sol: I understood immediately why he’d added those words.

hunks.baseline: *So not So Gyo. No—more precisely, he doesn’t know, either.*
hunks.sol: *So not So Gyo. No—he doesn’t know about her, either.*

hunks.baseline: There was no doubt.
Even Ma Sanbao, who was no longer among the living, and Cang Gong seemed not to know.
hunks.sol: It had to be that. Ma Sanbao hadn’t seemed to know, and neither had Cang Gong.

hunks.baseline: Who that mysterious woman was, or what she had in mind.
hunks.sol: Who was that woman? What was she thinking?

hunks.baseline: And unknown variables like her meant danger.
hunks.sol: An unknown like that meant danger.

hunks.baseline: *…Shit. Good thing I left the kids behind.*
hunks.sol: *…Fuck. Good thing I left the kids behind.*

hunks.baseline: I muttered to myself and raised the ownerless spear I’d picked up moments ago, aiming it at the enemies surging toward us.
hunks.sol: I raised the ownerless spear I’d picked up moments ago and aimed it at the enemies surging toward us.

hunks.baseline: I thought of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members who were probably waiting somewhere safe, expecting the Murim Alliance reinforcements that weren’t coming.
hunks.sol: I thought of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, who should be somewhere safe, waiting for Murim Alliance reinforcements that weren’t coming.

hunks.baseline: They’d probably make a huge fuss later, parroting “Captain” over and over. Still, if they’d stayed here, they’d have been dead by now. Or at least, it wouldn’t have been surprising if they were.
hunks.sol: They’d probably kick up a fuss later, repeating “Captain” like parrots. But if they’d stayed here, it wouldn’t have been surprising if they were already dead—

hunks.baseline: “Captain!”
hunks.sol: “Captaiiin!”

hunks.baseline: What the hell?
hunks.sol: What the fuck?

hunks.baseline: I turned around, feeling as though I’d been possessed by a ghost, and spotted familiar faces appearing in the distance.
hunks.sol: I turned, feeling as though I’d heard a ghost, and spotted familiar faces in the distance.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, I saw Hyuk Mujin at the head of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, hollering at the top of his lungs.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin was at the head of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, hollering at the top of his lungs.

hunks.baseline: And countless black figures trailing behind him like a tail.
hunks.sol: And countless black figures trailed behind them like a tail.
